'''Adina Merenlender''' (born October 1, 1963) is a Professor of [[Cooperative State Research, Education, and Extension Service|Cooperative Extension]] in Conservation Science at University of California, Berkeley in the Environmental Science, Policy, and Management Department, and is an internationally recognized [[Conservation biology|conservation biologist]] known for [[land-use planning]], [[Watershed management|watershed science]], [[landscape connectivity]], and [[Natural history|naturalist]] and [[stewardship]] training.

== Early life and education ==
Merenlender was born in Seattle, Washington and raised in West Los Angeles, California.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |title=Adina Merenlender |url=https://ucanr.edu/people/adina-merenlender |access-date=2025-12-04 |website=ucanr.edu |language=en-US}}</ref>

Merenlender graduated from [[University of California, San Diego|UC California San Diego]] in 1985 with a BA in Biology, where she also received her MS from the Department of Ecology and Evolutionary Biology in 1986.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|title=Adina MERENLENDER|url=https://ourenvironment.berkeley.edu/people/adina-merenlender|access-date=2021-07-05|website=Our Environment at Berkeley|language=en}}</ref> As a senior at UCSD, after listening to a seminar given on conservation by David Woodruff, she was inspired and switched her focus to [[Conservation genetics|conservation genetics.]] From there, she was involved in studying African rhinoceroses in collaboration with Oliver Ryder at the [[San Diego Zoo|San Diego Zoo.]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Q&A with SCB President-elect Adina Merenlender |url=https://conbio.org/publications/scb-news-blog/qa-with-scb-president-elect-adina-merenlender |access-date=2026-10-08 |website=conbio.org |language=en}}</ref> She was a visiting graduate student at [[Princeton University]] from 1987 to 1993,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Dobson Lab People|url=http://dobber.princeton.edu/People.html|access-date=2021-07-05|website=dobber.princeton.edu}}</ref> and she graduated from the [[University of Rochester]] in 1993 with a PhD in Biology.<ref name=":3" />

== Career ==
After earning her PhD in Biology, Merenlender did her post-doctoral fellowship at the Center for Conservation Biology at Stanford University from 1993 to 1995,<ref name=":4">{{Cite web|title=Home Page - Division of Agriculture and Natural Resources|url=https://ucanr.edu/?facultyid=1521|access-date=2021-07-05|website=ucanr.edu}}</ref> researching riparian plant and aquatic insect communities on Great Basin working lands under different livestock grazing regimes.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Kennedy|first1=Tom B.|last2=Merenlender|first2=Adina M.|last3=Vinyard|first3=Gary L.|title=A Comparison of Riparian Condition and Aquatic Invertebrate Community Indices in Central Nevada|date=2000|journal=Western North American Naturalist|volume=60|issue=3|pages=255–272|jstor=41717042|issn=1527-0904}}</ref> She started her career at UC Berkeley as Assistant Cooperative Extension Specialist and adjunct professor in 1995, at which time she moved to Mendocino County to conduct research at the UC Hopland Research and Extension Center, a 5,358-acre field station.<ref name=":4" />

Upon arriving in California's wine country, Merenlender conducted some of the first research in [[Vinecology]],<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Viers|first1=Joshua H.|last2=Williams|first2=John N.|last3=Nicholas|first3=Kimberly A.|last4=Barbosa|first4=Olga|last5=Kotzé|first5=Inge|last6=Spence|first6=Liz|last7=Webb|first7=Leanne B.|last8=Merenlender|first8=Adina|last9=Reynolds|first9=Mark|date=2013-03-15|title=Vinecology: pairing wine with nature|journal=Conservation Letters|volume=6|issue=5|pages=287–299|doi=10.1111/conl.12011|issn=1755-263X|doi-access=free|bibcode=2013ConL....6..287V |hdl=10533/148567|hdl-access=free}}</ref> the integration of ecological and viticultural practice to produce solutions for wine production and nature conservation.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Heaton|first1=Emily|last2=Merenlender|first2=Adina M.|date=May 2000|title=Modeling vineyard expansion, potential habitat fragmentation|journal=California Agriculture|volume=54|issue=3|pages=12–19|doi=10.3733/ca.v054n03p12|issn=0008-0845|doi-access=free}}</ref> Merenlender continues to advance conservation.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal|last1=Kremen|first1=C.|last2=Merenlender|first2=A. M.|date=2018-10-18|title=Landscapes that work for biodiversity and people|journal=Science|volume=362|issue=6412|article-number=eaau6020|doi=10.1126/science.aau6020|pmid=30337381|s2cid=53012788|issn=0036-8075|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Muñoz-Sáez|first1=Andrés|last2=Kitzes|first2=Justin|last3=Merenlender|first3=Adina M.|date=2020-08-20|title=Bird-friendly wine country through diversified vineyards|journal=Conservation Biology|volume=35|issue=1|pages=274–284|doi=10.1111/cobi.13567|pmid=32510666|s2cid=219538145|issn=0888-8892 |url=https://repositorio.uchile.cl/handle/2250/177598 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Muñoz-Sáez|first1=Andrés|last2=Heaton|first2=Emily E.|last3=Reynolds|first3=Mark|last4=Merenlender|first4=Adina M.|date=September 2020|title=Agricultural adapters from the vineyard landscape impact native oak woodland birds|journal=Agriculture, Ecosystems & Environment|volume=300|article-number=106960|doi=10.1016/j.agee.2020.106960|bibcode=2020AgEE..30006960M |s2cid=219523329|issn=0167-8809|doi-access=free}}</ref> Her work across California's North Coast vineyard landscape also includes watershed studies, revealing ways to avoid summer water withdrawals from streams to irrigate wine grapes, which is a necessary step to recovering California's salmon runs.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Grantham|first1=T. E.|last2=Mezzatesta|first2=M.|last3=Newburn|first3=D. A.|last4=Merenlender|first4=A. M.|title=Evaluating Tradeoffs Between Environmental Flow Protections and Agricultural Water Security|date=2013-01-24|journal=River Research and Applications|volume=30|issue=3|pages=315–328|doi=10.1002/rra.2637|s2cid=59143072 |issn=1535-1459}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Grantham|first1=Theodore E.|last2=Newburn|first2=David A.|last3=McCarthy|first3=Michael A.|last4=Merenlender|first4=Adina M.|date=May 2012|title=The Role of Streamflow and Land Use in Limiting Oversummer Survival of Juvenile Steelhead in California Streams|journal=Transactions of the American Fisheries Society|volume=141|issue=3|pages=585–598|doi=10.1080/00028487.2012.683472|bibcode=2012TrAFS.141..585G |issn=0002-8487}}</ref>

Merenlender led the earliest inquiries into the realized conservation benefits, or lack thereof, from conservation easements which spurred a large and still-growing body of scholarship on the topic.<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal|last1=Merenlender|first1=A. M.|last2=Huntsinger|first2=L.|last3=Guthey|first3=G.|last4=Fairfax|first4=S. K.|date=February 2004|title=Land Trusts and Conservation Easements: Who Is Conserving What for Whom?|journal=Conservation Biology|volume=18|issue=1|pages=65–76|doi=10.1111/j.1523-1739.2004.00401.x|bibcode=2004ConBi..18...65M |s2cid=35032260 |issn=0888-8892}}</ref> She also provided some of the first evidence for the impacts of quiet recreation on meso-carnivores and sparked continued field research into recreation management to minimize these impacts.<ref name=":2">{{Cite journal|last1=Reed|first1=Sarah E.|last2=Merenlender|first2=Adina M.|date=2008-06-28|title=Quiet, Nonconsumptive Recreation Reduces Protected Area Effectiveness|journal=Conservation Letters|volume=1|issue=3|pages=146–154|doi=10.1111/j.1755-263x.2008.00019.x|bibcode=2008ConL....1..146R |s2cid=13424093 |issn=1755-263X}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=REED|first1=SARAH E.|last2=Merenlender|first2=ADINA M.|date=2011-02-10|title=Effects of Management of Domestic Dogs and Recreation on Carnivores in Protected Areas in Northern California|journal=Conservation Biology|volume=25|issue=3|pages=504–513|doi=10.1111/j.1523-1739.2010.01641.x|pmid=21309853|bibcode=2011ConBi..25..504R |s2cid=15048789 |issn=0888-8892}}</ref>

Merenlender started the California Naturalist Program<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ucanr.edu/blogs/blogcore/postdetail.cfm?postnum=21183|title = Adina Merenlender: Building a new mode of extension for biodiversity conservation}}</ref> and served as its founding director.<ref name=":4" /><ref>{{Cite web|title=Leadership Team - UC California Naturalist|url=http://calnat.ucanr.edu/About_the_program/leadership/|access-date=2021-07-05|website=calnat.ucanr.edu}}</ref> Building on the success of this program, Merenlender helped start the first public education and service program on climate stewardship,<ref>{{Cite web|title=About UC Climate Stewards - UC California Naturalist|url=http://calnat.ucanr.edu/cs/cs_about/|access-date=2021-07-05|website=calnat.ucanr.edu}}</ref> including writing ''Climate Stewardship: Taking Collective Action to Protect California'' with [[Brendan Buhler]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ucanr.edu/blogs/blogcore/postdetail.cfm?postnum=43559|title = UC California Naturalist Program launches UC Climate Stewards}}</ref><ref name=":5">{{Cite book|url=https://www.ucpress.edu/book/9780520378940/climate-stewardship|title=Climate Stewardship|date=September 2021|isbn=978-0-520-37894-0|language=en|last1=Merenlender|first1=Adina|last2=Buhler|first2=Brendan|publisher=Univ of California Press }}</ref> The two programs provide [[collective impact]] on [[ecological health]] through community and [[citizen science]], contributed to by over 10,000 certified naturalists and climate stewards.

In 2004, Merenlender was a [[visiting scholar]] at the [[University of Queensland]] Department of Zoology in Brisbane, Australia. She was also a visiting scholar at the [[National Autonomous University of Mexico]] (UNAM) in Mexico City in 2008, and with the Cambridge Conservation Initiative through the [[University of Cambridge]] Zoology Department in 2019.<ref name=":4" />

As president, Merenlender worked with the Governing Board and staff to reorganize the [[Society for Conservation Biology|Society of Conservation Biology]] as a global network to preserve [[biodiversity]].

In 2005, Merelender co-authored Economics and Land Change in Prioritizing Private Land Conservation, published in Society of Conservation Biology.<ref>{{Cite journal | last1=Newburn | first1=David | last2=Reed | first2=Sarah | last3=Berck | first3=Peter | last4=Merenlender | first4=Adina |title=Economics and Land-Use Change in Prioritizing Private Land Conservation | journal=Conservation Biology | date=2005 | volume=19 | issue=5 | pages=1411–1420 |url=https://conbio.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/epdf/10.1111/j.1523-1739.2005.00199.x |language=en |doi=10.1111/j.1523-1739.2005.00199.x |issn=1523-1739|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

Now, Merenlender continues to make strides in the field of Environmental Science and Policy & Management at UC Berkley. She's currently leading multiple projects that maps, models, and monitors natural resources along side land use patterns by humans.<ref name=":6" />

'''Merenlender’s conservation work includes the use of spatially explicit decision-support systems for conservation planning.'''<ref>{{Cite web |title=Cooperative Extension {{!}} Rausser College of Natural Resources |url=https://nature.berkeley.edu/cooperative-extension |access-date=2026-10-17 |website=nature.berkeley.edu}}</ref>

* Section Editor, journal, [[PLOS One|''PlosOne'']]<ref>{{Cite web|title=PLOS ONE: accelerating the publication of peer-reviewed science|url=https://journals.plos.org/plosone/s/section-editors|access-date=2021-07-05|website=journals.plos.org}}</ref>

== Published works ==
Merenlender has published over 100 scientific research articles on the relationships between land use and biodiversity,<ref name=":4" /> and co-authored a book on [[wildlife corridor]] planning, ''Corridor Ecology: The science and practice of linking landscapes for biodiversity conservation'',<ref>{{Cite web|title=Corridor Ecology, Second Edition|url=https://islandpress.org/books/corridor-ecology-second-edition|access-date=2021-02-16|website=Island Press|date=19 October 2018 |language=en}}</ref> with the first edition published in 2006 and the second in 2019. She also co-authored ''The California Naturalist Handbook'',<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://www.ucpress.edu/book/9780520274808/the-california-naturalist-handbook|title=The California Naturalist Handbook|date=February 2013|isbn=978-0-520-27480-8|language=en|last1=Nevers|first1=Greg de|last2=Edelman|first2=Deborah Stanger|last3=Merenlender|first3=Adina|publisher=University of California Press }}</ref> now in its second edition,<ref>{{Cite web |title=The California Naturalist Handbook, Second Edition by Greg de Nevers, Deborah Edelman, Adina Merenlender - Paper |url=https://www.ucpress.edu/books/california-naturalist-handbook-second-edition/paper |access-date=2025-12-04 |website=University of California Press |language=en}}</ref> and ''Climate Stewardship: Taking Collective Action to Protect California''.<ref name=":5" />
